title: Milena Sova — Foundry widows' committee
content:
## Milena Sova

**Chair of the Kravenstal Foundry Widows' Committee. Widow of a casting-floor worker. Age 55.**

Widow of Pavol Sova, who worked the casting floor at Kravenstal for twenty-two years and died of foundry lung disease after the injury pensions were frozen in 1959. She chairs the committee that speaks for the district's widows, and she carries her husband's union card to every meeting. The committee keeps its own register of families affected by the illness, and the Chancellery has found no fuller list in the district.

Her request is specific. She wants the Lower Kraven Clinic, closed in 1961 and since sold to a company that never opened it, reopened and staffed by union medics. The file notes that she distrusts costings and budget offices, having heard their language all her life, and that she asks for a working door rather than a plan. Her committee has already written down the families who would use it.

**Voice:** Plain and unsentimental. She refuses to be thanked for listening and returns again and again to the same concrete request.

title: Vesna Darko — Korengal Valley land committee
content:
## Vesna Darko

**Speaker for the Korengal Valley land committee. Border farmer. Age 48.**

Farms the lower terraces of the valley below the Korengal Pass, on land her family held in writing from before the first border treaty. In the autumn of 1957 Halvek's garrison requisitioned the valley farms for the ridge fortification line, and eleven families were given a week to leave. Her family was never paid, and she now speaks for those who were moved.

The file notes that the families rent their own fields back from the garrison, paying a fee to plough the terraces they worked before the requisition, and that the lease is withdrawn when the fee is late. She keeps the 1958 and 1959 claims in a folder, each stamped as received and never answered. The survey sheets, she says, show that half the requisitioned land was never used.

**Voice:** Formal and documentary. She speaks in dates and signatures, and she trusts paper that can be read aloud in a schoolhouse more than promises from men in uniform or in good suits.

title: Gustav Wrenn — Wrenn Maritime
content:
## Gustav Wrenn

**Heir to the Wrenn shipping fortune. Quick and capable. Age 59.**

Heir to one of the old Amber Coast shipping fortunes, which prospered under Halvek. He grew up on the Aldenmoor harbour, where his father shipped salt cod from the berths when the basin held four hundred hulls. He is fast, well prepared and impatient with sentiment about the quay, which his office regards as a point in his favour.

His proposal asks for a twenty-year operating concession on the processing halls, with the tax relief that goes with it, and promises the halls rebuilt within eighteen months. Rumours persist in the corridors that Wrenn Maritime made payments to Halvek-era deputies while the family's contracts were most valuable. The file records these as rumour and nothing more.

**Voice:** Confident and businesslike. He argues from timetables and tonnage, and he says plainly when he thinks someone is wasting his afternoon.

title: Ana Kovar — Aldenmoor Fishermen's Cooperative
content:
## Ana Kovar

**Chair of the Aldenmoor Fishermen's Cooperative. Plain-spoken coastal organiser. Age 46.**

Chairs the cooperative that answers for four hundred boats and the families who crew them. She has no capital of her own and says so without apology. The members built the small cannery they now use with their own hands after the old one closed, and it needs rebuilding with a state loan before it can take the catch on a larger scale.

Her plan is slower than the Wrenn proposal, and she estimates three years rather than eighteen months. She wants the processing income to stay in Aldenmoor with the people who catch the fish, so that the boats work for the harbour rather than renting space in it. The file notes that she has put her timetable in writing and has not dressed it up as anything faster.

**Voice:** Direct and unhurried. She names her weaknesses before anyone else can, and she tends to close an argument by stating a figure and a date.

title: Dr. Ulrich Kessler — Kessler-Tyvar Mining Consortium
content:
## Dr. Ulrich Kessler

**Tyvaren industrialist. Head of the Consortium's Veltrian bid. Age 51.**

A Tyvaren industrialist who presents the Consortium's proposals in person, with the composure of a man who has rehearsed the first minute and found that it went well. The Consortium offers capital, pumps, a rail link to the border and engineers to run the shafts, and it promises to hire from the valley first. The file notes that he is courteous, extremely well briefed and seldom needs his papers.

His government watches each stage of his negotiations in Veltria, and he has said so openly. He adds that a signed Veltrian contract would be read in Tyvar as goodwill, returned in trade and in the border crossings closed for three years. The file records that he does not present this as a condition. Whether that interest is reassurance or pressure is not yet settled.

**Voice:** Courteous, precise and anticipatory. He answers the question before it is asked, and he frames each offer with a reason the other side can trust. He does not raise his voice.

title: Marta Ruzicka — Veltrian Ore Trust
content:
## Marta Ruzicka

**Runs the Veltrian Ore Trust. Domestic ore trader. Age 57.**

Runs the Veltrian Ore Trust, the domestic concern that bids for the Halden Valley shafts with a state loan as its only capital. She is proud, with some justice, that the Trust has never shipped ore it did not dig itself. Its ore goes to the Kravenstal foundries that make the steel for the country's rail. She sits with her hands folded on a ledger, as if expecting to be asked about the figures.

She is a little bitter about always being the smaller bid, and she does not hide it. Her proposal offers two years and a state loan to shore up the galleries. She will promise no ore to any buyer before explaining how the galleries are being made safe. The file records her point that the Trust will still be Veltrian when the Consortium's government has changed its mind.

**Voice:** Dry and exact, with a steady undertone of grievance that she keeps well under control. She counts tonnes and years rather than promises.

title: Oskar Halm — Dravenni miners' elder
content:
## Oskar Halm

**Elder of the Halden Valley miners. Thirty years underground. Age 64.**

Has spent thirty years underground in the Halden Valley, in the three iron mines that now stand closed above the town. His father dug the same shafts under another name, and the file records his view that the money from them left the valley on the same trains that carried the ore out. He speaks rarely, and he is the one the miners of the valley listen to.

His condition is practical rather than sentimental. He wants Dravenni foremen, not only Dravenni labourers, and he wants the men of the valley to have a voice in the timbering, the blasting and the decision about which galleries are safe to work. The file notes that nobody in the room argued with the request.

**Voice:** Spare and deliberate. He states a single condition and then stops, leaving the silence for others to fill.
